messages:
nina_sales: Heads-up: Nimbus Pharma wants a short connectivity pack for Private deployment POC. Key asks: PrivateLink vs peering, static egress (allowlisting), firewall ports and FQDNs, TLS inspection policy, Azure support, and any compliance/SOC2 blockers. Need to send by EOD.

sam_neteng: Quick take: recommend PrivateLink / Private Endpoint for initial POC. Pros: minimal route exposure, SG-level restrictions, easier rollback. Peering only if they need VPC-level routing for integrations.

harry_solutions: Static egress options: 1) Customer-owned NAT + EIP/PIP (fastest, preferred for regulated customers). 2) Redwood Reserved Egress IPs (addon + per-IP fee, provisioning ~3-7 business days). For a 2-4 week POC ask Nimbus to provide EIPs to avoid provisioning lead time.

li_sec: TLS inspection: we do NOT perform TLS MITM by default. If Nimbus requires corporate TLS inspect, recommend customer-managed forward proxy in their egress path. Any request for Redwood-managed interception requires legal/compliance signoff and will add weeks. Call out cert-pinning and mobile SDK breakage risks.

sam_neteng: Firewall snippet for ticket (pasteable):
- Allow inbound from Redwood PrivateLink ENI IPs or peered CIDR:
  - TCP 443 -> service endpoint IPs (required)
  - TCP 80 -> optional (health checks)
  - UDP 123 -> optional (NTP)
  - ICMP -> optional (diagnostics)
If using peering: add route table entry for our peering CIDR and lock SGs to the service subnets.

harry_solutions: FQDNs if they insist: api.redwood-inference.net, telemetry.redwood-inference.net. Note: FQDN allowlists are less deterministic for interface endpoints; prefer IP allowlist.

li_sec: DDoS and rate limits: Nimbus should rely on cloud provider DDoS protection (AWS Shield/Azure DDoS). We offer per-route throttling and request-level rate limiting but no managed scrubbing. Include that in questionnaire response.

sam_neteng: Azure note: we support Azure Private Endpoint. Customer should create the endpoint and approve the private link service connection. We do not create NICs in customer subscriptions without explicit setup.

harry_solutions: Pricing ask: two static egress IPs for a 4-week POC: recommend we quote prorated Reserved Egress addon if Nimbus wants us to manage IPs. I'll draft SOW language with an optional line: "Customer-provided EIPs recommended; Redwood-reserved EIPs available at additional cost and lead time."

li_sec: Compliance blockers to call out to customer: SOC2/HIPAA customers should prefer customer-owned egress for auditability. Any request for Redwood to manage egress IPs or TLS interception triggers compliance review.

ops-bot: Provision log: test connector created (connector-99) in us-west-2 at 2026-03-12T08:22:10Z.

nina_sales: Action items: @sam_neteng create 1-page connectivity diagram + allowlist template; @harry_solutions draft SOW blurb with prorated POC pricing; @li_sec prepare TLS inspection wording for their security team. I'll send to Nimbus once assembled.

sam_neteng: I'll upload the one-pager and CIDR list by EOD.

harry_solutions: Draft SOW line ready in 24h.

li_sec: I'll add a short paragraph on BYOK/KMS options if they ask about key control.

nina_sales: Thanks team. Flagging potential lead-time blocker: if Nimbus asks Redwood to provision reserved egress + permit TLS MITM, expect 2-4 week delay. Closing thread for now.
